correctness.rationale: For all integers q,n>=2, the graph has balanced degrees and explicit paths to and from the all-zero vertex. Its Laplacian is qI-B minus the embedded (q-1)-ary Laplacian; the de Bruijn walk identity B^m=J gives an exact restricted resolvent, and the smaller Laplacian annihilates the all-ones correction. Thus the determinant polynomial is proved for all parameters, not inferred from finite checks. Directed matrix-tree and fixed-edge BEST give the claimed rotation-class count, with no missing factorial or period quotient. An exact independent verifier checks cofactors, characteristic values, and small Euler tour counts.

originality.rationale: Full-text comparison with Leitner–Godbole and Blanca–Godbole identifies pre-existing existence of the same restricted-word cycles, explicitly credited. Direct comparisons with Sawada–Gabrić and indexed related exact tour counts do not yield the full one-required-symbol Laplacian characteristic polynomial or the all-q,n product. The exact count and spectral factorization remain provisionally original, subject to literature-index and inaccessible-paper risks.
residual_risks: An older unindexed analysis of single-required-letter de Bruijn Laplacians may already contain this determinant and product.
A general formula for restricted Eulerian tours may specialize without prominently naming the required-symbol language.
One closely related published exact-enumeration record could not be read in full; available description imposes a different bounded-weight condition.
Some secondary sources and the 2020 exact-enumeration article were assessed only from abstracts or short indexed summaries.

value.rationale: The natural required-letter/password universal-cycle family was previously known to exist but lacked a verified explicit count in the inspected sources. A closed all-alphabet, all-order product and full three-point Laplacian spectrum quantify the entire configuration space and permit exact global enumeration without an exponentially sized determinant. This is structurally beyond a one-parameter calculation; the binary equality with ordinary de Bruijn counts is a consistency boundary rather than the sole motivation.
